2610.07614.title: BioStudyBench: Evaluating Agents on Post-Cutoff Biomedical Studies
2610.07614.paper_summary: We evaluate whether AI agents can match the reported findings of published biomedical studies using public data. Existing evaluations do not consistently separate analysis from prior knowledge or retrieval of the published answer. We introduce BioStudyBench, a benchmark of 25 long-horizon analysis tasks drawn from studies first published between July and September 2026, after the developer-reported knowledge cutoffs of the models we evaluate, semi-automatically filtered down from 404,019 PubMed records. In each task, the agent receives a neutral research question but no data files, so it must find and download the relevant public data, search the literature through tools that return only records dated before its cutoff, and report findings through data analysis. To measure gains over prior knowledge, we run every task both with and without access to data and tools. Across eight models, access to data and tools raises the pass rate by 47 percentage points on average over the no-data baseline. Open-weight models across sizes trail closed-weight models, with the best open-weight model passing 81.3% of tasks against 94.7% for the best closed-weight model.
2610.07614.paper_summary_zh: 我們評估 AI 代理是否能夠使用公共數據匹配已發表生物醫學研究的報告結果。現有的評估並未一致區分分析與先前知識或檢索已發表答案。我們引入 BioStudyBench，這是一個基準，包含 25 個長期分析任務，這些任務來自於 2026 年 7 月至 9 月之間首次發表的研究，這些研究是在我們評估的模型的開發者報告的知識截止日期之後，並從 404,019 條 PubMed 記錄中半自動篩選而來。在每個任務中，代理會收到一個中立的研究問題，但沒有數據文件，因此它必須找到並下載相關的公共數據，通過僅返回截止日期之前的記錄的工具搜索文獻，並通過數據分析報告結果。為了衡量相對於先前知識的增益，我們在有和沒有數據及工具的情況下運行每個任務。在八個模型中，獲得數據和工具的情況下，通過率平均提高了 47 個百分點，相較於無數據的基準。不同大小的開放權重模型落後於封閉權重模型，最佳的開放權重模型通過了 81.3% 的任務，而最佳的封閉權重模型則為 94.7%。
